html:
Porter is the name archaeologists give to the Middle Woodland people of the Gulf coast of Alabama and Mississippi and the lower Tombigbee and Alabama rivers, around Mobile Bay. On this map it covers about 100 BCE to 500 CE.

Little is written about Porter for general readers. Its people fished, gathered shellfish and hunted along the coast and rivers. Their pottery and burial mounds tie them to the Marksville culture to the west and the Swift Creek people to the east, and through them to the wide Hopewell exchange network. Inland, up the Tombigbee, lived the Miller people.
